questions.question: What colour are the zig-zag lines at a zebra or pelican crossing?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 uses white zig-zag lines on both sides of crossings.

questions.question: What colour are the criss-cross lines of a box junction?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 marks box junctions with yellow criss-cross lines.

questions.question: When driving faster than 30 mph, what should you do when overtaking a cyclist?
options: Leave even more space than 1.5 metres
Pass closer so it takes less time
Sound your horn just before passing
questions.explain: Rule 163: Giving cyclists even more room at speeds over 30 mph.

questions.question: How do you check the two-second rule while driving?
options: Count two seconds after the car ahead passes a fixed landmark
Leave two car lengths at every speed
questions.explain: Rule 126: Counting two seconds from a fixed point the car ahead passes.

questions.question: What should you do with your indicator after completing a turn?
options: Make sure it cancels straight away
questions.explain: Rule 103: To cancel your signal after finishing the turn so it does not mislead.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit for a car on a UK motorway. Unless signs show lower?
questions.explain: Rule 124: The motorway limit for cars is 70 mph.

questions.question: May you creep forward over the white line while red and amber are showing?
options: No, stay behind the stop line until green
questions.explain: Rule 175: Crossing the white line on red. Amber is still jumping the red light.

questions.question: Before joining a busier road from a give-way line, where should you look?
options: Both right and left for vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians
questions.explain: Rule 172: To look both ways for all road users before pulling out.

questions.question: If a pedestrian has already stepped into the road you are turning into. What must you do?
questions.explain: Rule 170: You must give way to pedestrians. Already crossing the road you are turning into.

questions.question: When should you switch on your left indicator before turning left?
options: In good time before slowing and turning
Only if a car is behind
questions.explain: Rule 182 and Rule 103 say to give a clear left signal in good time.

questions.question: When changing lanes, how should your move affect vehicles in the next lane?
options: They should slow down slightly for you
You must not force them to slow down or swerve
You only need to clear cars behind you
You have priority if you signal first
questions.explain: Rule 133: You must not cut in or force others to slow down.

questions.question: When may you move onto the right-hand side of a two-way road?
options: When overtaking or passing a parked vehicle safely
questions.explain: Rule 160: You only move right when overtaking. Passing an obstruction, or turning right, and when it is safe.

questions.question: When is it safe to enter a roundabout?
options: When there is a safe gap so circulating traffic does not have to slow down
Whenever you reach the line first
Whenever the car in front enters, without looking
Only after stopping for three seconds
questions.explain: Rule 185: Entering only when there is a safe gap to the right.

questions.question: What signal should you give on approach when going straight ahead at a roundabout?
questions.explain: Rule 186: Not to signal on approach when going straight ahead.

questions.question: When turning right at a roundabout, what should you do with your signal before leaving?
options: Keep signalling right until you are on the new road
Switch from right signal to left signal just after the exit before yours
questions.explain: Rule 186: To signal left after passing the exit before your right-turn exit.

questions.question: Which blue sign warns you to keep left of a roundabout island?
options: A blue circle with white arrows pointing clockwise
A red triangle with a cross
questions.explain: Rule 185: The blue mini-roundabout and roundabout arrows showing clockwise flow.

questions.question: Where must a car driver stop on red when there is an advanced stop line?
options: Behind the first white line before the cycle box
questions.explain: Rule 178: You must stop at the first white line. So the cycle box stays clear for cyclists.

questions.question: In Great Britain, may you turn left at. A red traffic light if the road is clear?
options: No, you must wait for green
Yes, if no pedestrians are waiting
questions.explain: Rule 175: Unlike some countries. There is no turn on red in Great Britain unless a green arrow shows.

questions.question: You want to turn right. An oncoming car is close. What should you do?
options: Wait behind the turn point until it passes
questions.explain: Rule 180: Give way to oncoming traffic before turning across it.

questions.question: What happens if you drift sideways out of your lane on a roundabout?
options: You could collide with a car or cyclist beside you
questions.explain: Rule 186: Against cutting across another driver's lane when circulating.

questions.question: If the car ahead of you stops at a stop line and moves off. What must you do when you reach the line?
options: Stop again at the white line yourself
questions.explain: Rule 171: Every vehicle must stop at the line in turn and check both ways.

questions.question: Why should you choose your roundabout approach lane early?
options: To avoid last-second swerving across other drivers
So you do not need signals
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 encourages early lane selection for smooth, safe driving.

questions.question: You are 40 metres away at 30 mph when the light turns amber. What should you do?
options: Brake smoothly and stop behind the line
questions.explain: Rule 175: At 30 mph. 40 metres is plenty of room to stop safely behind the line.

questions.question: If there is a central refuge island on a zebra crossing, how is it treated?
questions.explain: Rule 195: A central island splits it into two separate crossings. Though you should still watch carefully.

questions.question: What kind of road marking goes with a stop sign?
options: A solid white line and stop painted on the road
questions.explain: Rule 171: A stop sign is paired with. A solid white stop line across your lane.

questions.question: At a roundabout with three approach lanes, the middle lane is marked straight ahead. Which lane should you use to go straight?
questions.explain: Rule 186: To follow painted lane markings on multi-lane approaches.

questions.question: You are two metres from the stop line at 30 mph. A car is close behind when the light turns amber. What should you do?
options: Stop in the middle of the junction
questions.explain: Rule 175: You are too close to stop safely. Continuing through is the safer choice.

questions.question: Where does the no-overtaking rule at a zebra crossing apply?
options: Within the zig-zag zone on the approach to the crossing
Only on the black and white stripes
Only after you pass the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 applies across the zig-zag markings approaching the crossing.

questions.question: The traffic light is green, but cars are queued just past the box junction. What should you do?
options: Drive into the box so cars behind you can cross
Wait behind the junction until space opens beyond the box
Sound your horn to make the queue move
questions.explain: Rule 174: You must wait. Before the box even on a green light if the exit is blocked.

questions.question: In wet or windy weather, how should you adjust your overtaking gap past a cyclist?
options: Leave even more space than usual
questions.explain: Rule 163: Extra clearance in poor weather or strong side winds.

questions.question: What happens to your view ahead when you leave a proper two-second gap?
options: You can see past the vehicle ahead and spot hazards earlier
You see less of the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 notes a wider gap improves your view of road hazards.

questions.question: Why could a late signal confuse other road users?
options: It gives them too little time to react safely
It breaks the speed limit rule
It turns off your brake lights
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 stresses signalling early enough for others to read and react.

questions.question: Can you drive above the speed limit briefly while overtaking?
options: Yes, for up to five seconds
No, you must never exceed the speed limit
Yes, if no cameras are nearby
questions.explain: Rule 124: Speed limits are the legal maximum at all times.

questions.question: Does a pedestrian pelican crossing show red and amber to drivers?
options: No, it goes from red to flashing amber, then green
questions.explain: Rule 196: Pelican crossings use flashing amber instead of red and amber.

questions.question: Why should you check carefully for cyclists and motorcycles at a T-junction?
options: They are narrower and easier to miss against background traffic
They must always stop for cars
questions.explain: Rule 172: Looking carefully for smaller, faster two-wheelers.

questions.question: Why should you not wave a pedestrian across when stopping at a junction?
options: Another vehicle may not see them or may overtake
questions.explain: Rule H2: Wait patiently without waving so the pedestrian checks for other traffic themselves.

questions.question: Why should you look over your shoulder before moving into another lane?
options: Because mirrors do not show every blind spot
To wave thank you to cars behind
To see if your brake lights work
questions.explain: Rule 133: Mirrors cannot cover every blind spot beside your car.

questions.question: Why should you not hug the centre line on a bend?
options: An oncoming vehicle could hit you
It is illegal to steer left
questions.explain: Rule 160: Keeping left gives oncoming traffic room. Especially where you cannot see round a bend.

questions.question: If a car on the roundabout is signalling left to take the exit before yours. What should you do?
options: Wait until you see it actually start turning off
Flash your lights to hurry it up
questions.explain: Rule 185: Not to rely on another driver's signal alone before pulling out.

questions.question: Which signal do you give on approach when going straight ahead (second exit)?
questions.explain: Rule 186: Not to signal on approach when going straight ahead.

questions.question: You are visiting from a right-hand-driving country. What habit must you watch at UK roundabouts?
options: Do not turn anti-clockwise onto the roundabout; keep left and go clockwise
Sound your horn at every exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 reminds newcomers that UK roundabouts always go clockwise.

questions.question: What should you do if a lorry beside. You needs extra width to turn on a roundabout?
options: Hold back and give the lorry plenty of room instead of sitting alongside it
Pull right beside its rear wheels
questions.explain: Rule 186: and 221 warn that long vehicles swing wide across lanes on roundabouts.

questions.question: What sign sits on the central island facing approaching traffic on many roundabouts?
options: A blue sign with white keep-left arrows or white chevrons pointing left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 uses keep-left arrows and chevrons to guide traffic clockwise.

questions.question: When two exit lanes merge after a roundabout, how should you leave?
options: Stay in your exit lane cleanly, then merge smoothly when safe
Squeeze both cars side by side into one lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 keeps exits orderly until lanes merge safely downstream.

questions.question: Why are zig-zag lines painted on both the approach and exit sides of a crossing?
options: To keep views clear in both directions and stop overtaking or parking near the stripes
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 keeps both sides of the crossing clear for pedestrians and drivers.

questions.question: Which turning direction has the special exception to wait inside a yellow box junction?
options: Turning right (when only oncoming traffic stops you)
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 grants the exception only for right turns blocked by oncoming traffic.

questions.question: On a 50 mph rural road. Why is 1.5 metres often not enough when passing a cyclist?
options: High speed creates strong air turbulence, so give even more room
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 explicitly requires even more space at speeds over 30 mph.

questions.question: Why is two seconds still too short behind a vehicle on a wet road?
options: Wet roads double stopping distance, so leave at least four seconds
Brakes lock faster in dry weather
Two seconds only applies to bikes
questions.explain: Rule 126: To double the gap to four seconds in wet weather.

questions.question: What should you check before cancelling a signal early if you change your mind?
options: That nobody has already reacted to your first signal
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 stresses clear, unambiguous signals at all times.

questions.question: What happens when variable gantry signs show a. Speed inside a red ring on a motorway?
options: That lower limit is legally enforced
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 and 258 make red-ring gantry limits legally binding.
